# dsh-officecli-connection
**English** · 中文
A thin DeepSeek Harness shell around a **locally installed** OfficeCLI binary.
The plugin ships no binary, downloads nothing, and updates nothing. You install OfficeCLI yourself;
the plugin only learns where it is and gives the agent a clean way to call it.
## What it adds
| Piece | Detail |
| Settings page | **Settings → OfficeCLI**: the binary path, and a Test button that reports the dete
cted version and how many guides are mounted. There is no "inject skills" switch: the guides *are* t
he workflow, so a tool without them would be an executor with no manual. Clearing the path is the wa

y to switch Office off. |
| `officecli` tool | One tool, parameter `command` (a command line or pre-
split argv). The process starts in the **session working directory**, so relative paths behave like

a shell. Rendered pages come back as image attachments. |
| Skills | OfficeCLI's ten bundled guides
(`pptx`, `word`, `excel`, `word-form`, `morph-ppt`, `morph-ppt-3d`, `pitch-deck`, `academic-paper`,
`data-dashboard`, `financial-model`) are exposed as runtime skills. Names follow the skill's own id,
so `word` surfaces as `officecli-docx` and `excel` as `officecli-xlsx` — the way the other skill bo
dies cross-reference them. One extra entry, `officecli-workflow`, is this plugin's own: it maps the
ten, states the engine boundary and carries the traps list (see *Coexisting with other Office skills
*). It is deliberately **not** named `officecli`, because the binary installs a base manual under th
at name — see *A second `officecli` skill* below. |
Skills are injected through the Harness skill-provider contract, so **no file is ever written anywhe
re**: no workspace, no `.agents/`, no `~/.claude`. The catalog comes from `officecli load_skill` and
a body from `officecli load_skill <slug>`, both of which print to stdout. Bundled reference files s
tay loadable through the skill's `resourceBase`, which tells the agent to run `officecli load_skill
<slug> --path <relpath>`.
[该节后续省略]
## Boundary: what happens to output
| Channel | Treatment |

| stdout | passed through verbatim as the text block, truncated at 8 MB |
| stderr | appended to tha

t text; never parsed, never dropped |
| exit code | passed through unchanged; no retry, no reinterpr

etation. `2` means "ran with caveats": read `warnings`, `success` can be false |
| a line naming an
existing image file | committed as a durable attachment and returned as an image block; over a deplo

yment size limit you get the path plus a note |
| everything else | untouched — no JSON parsing, no
HTML rendering, no file watching |
The tool description deliberately carries **no flag reference**. It tells the model to run `officecl
i help`, `help <verb>` and `help <format> <element>`, because the binary is the authoritative schema
and any hardcoded flag list drifts with the version. What it does carry is the short list of traps
below — the ones that cost a real document build.
## Known upstream behaviour
Reproduced against OfficeCLI 1.0.158. None of this is the plugin's own design; the tool description
repeats it so the model does not rediscover it on every document.
| Behaviour | What to do |
| The binary runs **argv, not a shell** | no `&&`, `\|`, `>`, `$VAR`; one command per call, or put t

he steps in `batch` |
| Long or non-ASCII arguments belong in a file | `batch <file> --input <json>`
; inline quoting breaks eventually and silently — a serialised argv array reaches the CLI as the lit

eral token `[batch,` |
| A bare length is EMU, not an error | `margin=26` collapses the box while `v

alidate` still passes; write `pt`/`cm`. `spacing` is the opposite: unitless points |
| `add` and `se
t` disagree on property names | `add` takes `w`/`h`, `set` takes `width`/`height`; a wrong name only

prints `UNSUPPORTED props`, and the call still exits 0 |
| `batch` rolls back on failure | one bad

item discards the others, yet the summary line still counts them as succeeded |
| Fonts are per scri

pt | set `font.latin` **and** `font.ea`; a lone `font` leaves CJK on a monospace fallback |
| Table
defaults are close to unusable | `border.all=none` plus `border.horizontal`, and an explicit header

fill, or the header text is invisible |
| Write verbs keep a resident process | another reader meanw

hile gets "being used by another process"; run `close <file>` when done |
| `validate` checks the pa
ckage, not the layout | a table can overflow the slide and still pass; only a screenshot shows it —

text that overflows a box is clipped or wrapped out of sight, at any font size |
[该节后续省略]
## Why not MCP
OfficeCLI's own `officecli mcp` server exposes exactly one tool whose only parameter is a command-li
ne string, so an MCP hop buys nothing here but adds a second process, a serialization quirk (array a
rguments arrive as a bracketed string), and an unconfigurable working directory. Registering the too
l directly lets the plugin spawn with `cwd` set to the session directory and re-read the configured
path on every call, so editing the path takes effect without a restart.
## Compatibility
There is deliberately no `engines.dsh` field: a version gate rejects builds that would have worked.
What the plugin needs is checked when it mounts, and only the three services without which it is poi
ntless are hard requirements.
| Piece | Needed? | If missing |
| `tools`, `subprocess`, `skills` host services | required | the plugin does not mount, and the erro

r names the missing service |
| `webServer` | optional | the tool and the guides still work; set the

path in `settings.json` |
| `attachments` | optional | rendered pages come back as file paths inste

ad of image attachments |
| `workingDirectory` | optional | the tool runs in the system temp directo

f image attachments |
| `workingDirectory` | optional | the tool runs in the system temp directory |
Tested against Harness `0.2.1-rc.2` on Windows with OfficeCLI 1.0.148–1.0.158. The same plugin code
was then exercised on Linux (WSL, Node 22, OfficeCLI 1.0.148): tool, skills provider, HTTP routes an
d command splitting all pass there.
